problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ -27\end{aligned}].
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{5t}\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system is

| $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+$

worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ -27\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also exponential, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}],
$$

where $a,b$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=-4{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ -27\end{aligned}] \\ -4[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ -27\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-4a \\ -4b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3a \\ 5b\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-14 \\ -27\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-4a \\ -4b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3a-14 \\ 5b-27\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3a-14=-4a \\ 5b-27=-4b\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get

$$
3a-14=-4a\,⇒\,a=2.
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
5b-27=-4b\,⇒\,b=3.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
